summary.headline: Menon Bearings FY26 consolidated PAT rose 53.41% to INR 38.25 crore; Q4 PAT up 108.55% YoY, with management guiding 20-22% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income above INR 300 crore (up 23.16% YoY), PAT of INR 38.25 crore (up 53.41%), and EPS rising from INR 4.45 to INR 6.83. Q4 consolidated PAT grew 108.55% YoY, and the company cited Q4 EBITDA of about 25%. Management guided to 25% annual volume growth, 20-22% EBITDA margin for the next two years, and INR 500 crore revenue by FY28. Alkop (aluminium) growth was flagged as a key swing factor after a slow prior two years.

financial_highlights.value: About 1.5x; Bearings about 2x, Alkop about 1.5x, Brakes about 1x
About 25% (per analyst recap, confirmed as correct by management)

segments.name: Bi-Metal bearings
segments.commentary: Utilisation reached about 85%; new business pipeline above INR 50 crore across 28-30 customers over the current and next two years. Growth guided at about 23-25% per year. Tractors about 35% of revenue, HCV/LCV 25%, brakes-use 25%, transmission 15%, other industrial about 10%.

segments.name: Aluminium (Alkop)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 25% QoQ; utilisation rose from 45% to 60% and is expected to reach 90% by year-end. Installed capacity 1,450 tpa with a spare holding furnace. Management guided 29% growth for the next two years and more than INR 120 crore revenue in two years. Pipeline of about INR 30 crore from 51 new parts.

segments.name: Brakes
segments.commentary: Capacity added by about 1 lakh pieces per month. Railway registration done, but no railway revenue yet; dynamometer delivery expected by August 2026. Brakes CapEx of INR 3 crore; pipeline of about INR 10 crore over two years.

segments.name: Exports and channel mix
segments.commentary: Exports about 35% of revenue; about 80% of export orders are ex-works. US exports rose about 50% YoY. Consolidated mix: auto 75%, other 25%. Order book about 60% export and 40% domestic.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: management said it expects to exceed INR 350 crore and estimates more than INR 360 crore.
Revenue target of INR 500 crore by FY28 at about 25% annual growth, described as optimistic and dependent on geopolitical conditions.
EBITDA margin to be sustained at 20-22% over the next two years on a conservative basis; Q4 level of about 25% was linked to export and high-volume mix.
Asset turnover to reach about 2x on a consolidated basis by FY28.
Planned CapEx of about INR 25 crore over two years for Bi-Metal, INR 7 crore for Alkop, and INR 3 crore for Brakes, mostly funded by internal accruals.
Raw material cost pass-through is quarterly and index-linked; one or two customers still to be moved to full pass-through in Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Bi-Metal CapEx INR 25 crore over two years; Alkop INR 7 crore; Brakes INR 3 crore; mostly internal accruals.
Alkop installed capacity 1,450 tpa, running at about 1,500 tpa output and 65% utilisation; a spare holding furnace can double capacity when needed, with another furnace expected next year.
Brakes dynamometer, a key railway qualification item, is expected by August 2026 after earlier delays from two other vendors.
Railway business expected to start from around August/end of 2026 at 5-10% of revenue initially.
demand_pricing: Order book reported at more than INR 32 crore; management expects to target about INR 190 crore in the next six months (as stated on the call).

Raw material costs (aluminium and copper) rose sharply; aluminium grade cost moved from INR 240/kg to INR 280/kg, copper about INR 1,275/kg, vs about INR 900 a year earlier. Pass-through is quarterly, index-linked.
Alkop average realisation about INR 700-750/kg against INR 200-250 value-add for competitors, per management. Alkop EBITDA margin about 20% vs 6-8% at large competitors, per management.
Export interest: European RFQs rising over the last six months; a PTFE bush opportunity for seven parts, with one sample approved, targeting about 6 lakh pieces per month.
Africa exports via Dubai halted for three months (about INR 2 crore lost), offset by about INR 6 crore of annual orders via a merchant exporter with advance payment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is interest expense high, and how will it be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Export debtor days exceed 180, raising working capital. Management is shifting to PCFC limits (INR 6 crore drawn at about 4.7% vs about 8% earlier; INR 25 crore total limit planned) with a 2.75% export interest subvention, targeting about 4% savings on working capital limit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory from operating leverage and export mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export pipeline (over 50% of new business) carries better margins, and it expects margin improvement above 15 bps in FY27. Q4 uplift was attributed to higher capacity utilisation: Bi-Metal at 85%, Alkop up from 45% to 60%, Brakes up by 1 lakh pieces per month.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Alkop lagged, and what drives its growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed export delays and customer slowdowns from the war, tariffs and raw material inflation, with samples delayed from January to March. It expects about 29% annual growth for Alkop over the next two years and says Alkop could match Bearings' revenue contribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin guidance and quarterly volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that EBITDA margin would likely range between 20% and 22% for the full year on a conservative basis, and that quarterly margins could move between 22% and 25% depending on export and high-volume mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance of INR 350 crore maintained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to exceed INR 350 crore and estimates more than INR 360 crore; it noted that FY26 had beaten the earlier INR 275 crore target and been revised to INR 290 crore.

risks_watch: Raw material pass-through lag: pass-through is quarterly and one or two customers are still not on full index-linked pricing, so margin can dip in the interim.
Export working capital: debtor days above 180 and about 80% of export orders still on DDP terms; Q1 FY27 receivables and interest cost need monitoring.
Alkop growth depends on order placement timing from John Deere, Taco Prestolite, Eaton, Honeywell and others. Management said orders are not yet firm.
Railway and brakes OEM entry depends on dynamometer commissioning by August 2026 and vendor registration.
Geopolitical risk: Middle East logistics congestion, Africa export halt, and possible export rerouting or customer pricing pressure.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and margin outlook; several answers were loosely quantified and some figures were restated on the call (for example, the revenue target, the Alkop tonnage and the CapEx split). Management was evasive on order book segment split and on the reason for the dynamometer delay.
key_quotes: I again assure you that considering the present situation going forward, we will be able to maintain EBITDA more than 20% and it should be about between 20 % to 22% during next two years.
So, we are not after volumes, we are balancing both the games, you see, volumes to the certain extent, which can fetch us margins which are sustainable.
Our management, everything working together, we have exceeded the number by INR 25 crore.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue above INR 360 crore, 25% annual growth and INR 500 crore by FY28, backed by Bi-Metal 85% utilisation, a INR 50 crore+ pipeline, INR 32 crore order book (targeting INR 190 crore in six months), and INR 35 crore capex, though the FY28 target is called optimistic.
